how_to_ingest: rag by section + checklist table; build templates/bfpme_*.json from the headings
caveats: Not in the zip: copy from the repo grants_and_financial_aids folder. Check the 2024 form is the latest.

dataset: GIZ business-plan model (creation/extension)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Donor-style plan template, useful as a second structure and for financial table layouts
how_to_ingest: template skeleton + xlsx financial layout
caveats: Repo file; confirm language version.

dataset: SBA business plan guide, Business Model Canvas page, Lean Canvas page
what_it_gives_the_plan: International reference structures (traditional 9 sections, 9-block BMC, 12-block lean canvas)
how_to_ingest: already turned into templates/sba_generic, bmc, lean_canvas
key_value_to_use: Lean Canvas page lists 12 blocks (this corpus page); BMC and Lean pages are thin marketing pages.
caveats: Marketing pages, not formal standards: cite as frameworks.

dataset: Code de l'IRPP et de l'IS (consolidated)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Corporate tax rate and exceptions, deductions, depreciation rules, minimum tax: drives the tax line of every projection
zip_ids: S065 (linked/S065_code_IS_et_IRPP_francais_1); the S065 DGI page is an empty capture
how_to_ingest: rag by ARTICLE + rules table (rate by activity)
key_value_to_use: General IS rate 20% (art. 49, LF 2024-48, profits from 1 Jan 2024); reduced rates e.g. 10% for artisanal/agri/fishing activities (see art. 49)
caveats: Zip edition stops at LF 2024. LF 2026 added contributions (see lf2026). The Damodaran file lists Tunisia at 15% and 25%: do not use it for tax.

dataset: Loi de finances 2026 (Law 2025-17 of 12 Dec 2025)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Newest tax and social parameters: solidarity contribution, e-invoicing duty, state support for hiring graduates, wage-increase framework
fetch_method: script for documents or secondary source + manual for the rest
how_to_ingest: rag by article; extract a parameters table (year, rule, value, article)
key_value_to_use: Employer CNSS reference rate 17.07% general regime and 16.57% totally exporting (per Deloitte summary); hiring support for higher-education graduates degressive from 100% to 20% over 5 years; electronic invoicing obligation extended to services; wage increases framework 2026-2028
caveats: Secondary source. Get the official text from the JORT (n. 148, 12 Dec 2025) before quoting rates in the report. A draft-bill summary mentioned a solidarity contribution of 3% or 4% of profits depending on the IS rate band: confirm the final text.

dataset: Code de la TVA (rates and exemptions)
what_it_gives_the_plan: VAT on sales and purchases, cash-flow timing, exempt activities
how_to_ingest: rules table (product/activity -> rate) + rag by article
caveats: Not in the zip. Standard and reduced rates must be read from the current code, not from memory.

dataset: Startup Act: Law 2018-20, Decree 2018-840, BCT circulars 2019-01 and 2019-02
publisher: Startup Tunisia / Ministry of Communication Technologies
what_it_gives_the_plan: Label criteria and the tax, payroll, FX and leave benefits that change a startup's projections
how_to_ingest: rag by article + eligibility rules table
key_value_to_use: 20 measures built around a label of merit; the portal lists the law, the decree and the two BCT circulars
caveats: Law texts live in the repo law/.../01_STARTUPS folder. Check the label criteria on the portal before encoding them.

dataset: Tunisian accounting framework: Law 96-112, SCE, conceptual framework, NCT 42 (simplified), NC 01 to NC 38
what_it_gives_the_plan: Structure of balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement; depreciation, inventory, leases, revenue rules: makes projected statements compliant
how_to_ingest: rag by standard and paragraph; statement layouts as tables
caveats: Standards come from the zip; keep the standard number and paragraph as the citation.

dataset: SMIG/SMAG minimum wage decree and 2026-2028 wage increases
what_it_gives_the_plan: Wage floor and yearly escalation for staffing costs
fetch_method: script for documents or secondary source + manual for the rest
how_to_ingest: parameters table (year, regime, amount)
key_value_to_use: Increases of 5% per year in 2026, 2027 and 2028 (SMIG and SMAG); published in JORT n. 44 of 30 April 2026 per press
caveats: Secondary source. Read the decree text for the exact monthly amounts and the 40h/48h regimes.

dataset: CNSS contribution rates and ceilings
what_it_gives_the_plan: Employer and employee social charges added to gross salary
how_to_ingest: parameters table (regime, employer rate, employee rate)
key_value_to_use: Employer reference rate 17.07% (general) and 16.57% (totally exporting) per Deloitte summary of LF 2026
caveats: Confirm on the CNSS site; some regimes rise with the SMIG.

dataset: BCT policy rate and TMM (monthly average money-market rate)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Base for bank loan interest assumptions and financing cost
fetch_method: manual (script fetches a press stand-in only)
zip_ids: S054 (TMM) and S055 (policy rate) are empty captures: need the real tables
how_to_ingest: time series table (month, rate)
key_value_to_use: Policy rate 7.00% (kept at the 11 Feb 2026 meeting; reported unchanged at 31 Jul 2026); TMM 6.99% Feb-Jul 2026 and 7.00% in Aug 2026 (press citing BCT). Check September 2026.
caveats: Bank lending rates to firms sit above the TMM: you need the spread from a bank offer or BCT lending-rate statistics.

dataset: BCT daily exchange rates (TND vs EUR, USD, others)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Cost of imported inputs and foreign revenue in TND; FX sensitivity scenario
how_to_ingest: time series table (date, currency, rate)
caveats: Rates are a single average rate without buy/sell spread (per press description): add a margin.

dataset: INS data portal: CPI inflation, GDP, employment, population by governorate
what_it_gives_the_plan: Inflation to escalate costs and prices, market size by region, labour market
format: web portal with API; csv export
zip_ids: S062 (INS yearbook page) is an empty capture
how_to_ingest: time series table by indicator and governorate
key_value_to_use: Portal has a data bank, an API and queries (INS leaflet)
caveats: Source documents are from 2014 to 2020; the INS site had reported website issues in 2024: test the portal and API live.

dataset: World Bank Open Data / WDI API for Tunisia
what_it_gives_the_plan: Long time series (GDP, inflation, credit to private sector, internet use, urbanisation) with a stable API
how_to_ingest: api pull into a long table
caveats: Example endpoint is GDP growth. Check the licence line on each dataset page.

dataset: Startup Tunisia annual reports (startup ID card, revenue, jobs, funding)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Real numbers on labelled Tunisian startups: revenue, headcount, funding: sanity checks for a startup's projections
how_to_ingest: extract tables to csv by year; rag for narrative
key_value_to_use: A press summary of the 2019-2020 report says 248 labelled startups generated about 66 million dinars of cumulative revenue
caveats: The 2020 FR report is the one I found; look for later years on the same portal.

dataset: World Bank Enterprise Surveys Tunisia (panel 2013, 2020, 2024)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Real Tunisian firm-level data: sales, employment, financing access, obstacles, by ISIC sector and size: reality checks for projections
fetch_method: script for documents or secondary source + manual for the rest
zip_ids: S077 Indicator Description pdf (in 07_firm_data/wbes); the S077 Tunisia page is an empty capture
how_to_ingest: firm table; compute medians by sector and size band
key_value_to_use: Panel file: 1,852 cases, 738 variables; the 2024 wave alone: 645 firms, 339 variables; sector variable d1a2 is ISIC Rev. 3.1
caveats: Microdata download needs a login and acceptance of terms. Sample sizes by sector can be small.

dataset: Nomenclature d'Activités Tunisienne (NAT) with correspondence to ISIC
what_it_gives_the_plan: Maps the founder's activity to a code so the right benchmarks are picked
how_to_ingest: mapping table NAT -> ISIC -> NACE -> Damodaran industry
caveats: Check which NAT edition is current.

dataset: ISIC Rev.4 and NACE Rev.2 correspondence tables
what_it_gives_the_plan: Lets you join WBES (ISIC 3.1), Eurostat (NACE) and Damodaran industries
how_to_ingest: mapping tables
caveats: Damodaran industries have no official code: you must build that mapping by hand once.

dataset: Damodaran: after-tax operating margin and ROC; cost of capital and betas; country risk premiums; country tax rates
what_it_gives_the_plan: Sector margin and cost-of-capital references, and a Tunisia country risk premium for discount rates
zip_ids: S067 (margins), S070 + S071 beta/totalbeta/wacc files for Europe, emerging, global, Japan, China, India, rest, S071 countrytaxrates and ctryprem (Apr26, Jul25, Jul26, Jun13)
how_to_ingest: tables: already loaded in 06_international_benchmarks/derived/benchmarks.sqlite (margins, wacc, country tax, country risk). Use the Emerging-market or Europe files first for a Tunisian plan
key_value_to_use: Tunisia: rating Caa1, country risk premium 9.28%, total equity risk premium 13.48% (July 2026 file in the zip)
caveats: US and global data, not Tunisian norms: always label the region. Tunisia tax rows (15% and 25%) conflict with the IS code.

dataset: Damodaran: gross and operating margins, working capital, capex and debt ratios by industry (Europe, emerging markets, global)
what_it_gives_the_plan: Fills what the zip lacks: gross margin, working-capital days, capex/sales, debt ratios: needed for cash-flow and funding-need lines
how_to_ingest: add tables to benchmarks.sqlite
caveats: Checked: the zip has NO gross-margin, working-capital, capex or debt files. File names margin.xls, wcdata.xls, capex.xls, dbtfund.xls are from memory (the folder URL is confirmed in the zip metadata): the download script logs any 404. Prefer Emerging Markets or Europe versions
